subject: HealthApt deployment: tenancy & SLO clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: HealthApt deployment: tenancy & SLO clarification and next steps

Hi Maria / Connor —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Production goal: clinical note summarization and search for US customers (PHI question pending).
- QPS & latency profile: 200 qps peak, 95th pct < 180ms target for read/short completions, batchable for bulk indexing jobs.
- Risk/concern: shared infrastructure/noisy neighbor effects, strict data isolation for certain workloads, and enterprise SLA needs.

What Redwood proposes for qualification:
1) Technical note from our infra team explaining isolation boundaries between Hosted (shared), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem) modes — will include KV cache isolation, multi-tenant scheduling behavior, and typical latency variability.
2) SLO table mapping: 99.9% availability targets, 95th/99th latency expectations per mode, and fallbacks (model variants/regions) we recommend.
3) Pricing & contract paths: quick worksheet for Dedicated vs Private one-time onboarding effort and recurring pricing bands.

Requested items from you to finalize recommendations:
- Confirm whether PHI will be processed in the initial pilot (this affects Private/VPC requirement).
- Any hard upper bound on allowed 99th latency during peak (if you have it).

Attachments I’m including with this message:
- redwood_sla_and_tenancy_brief.pdf (short explainer of modes + SLO examples)
- pricing-worksheet-healthapt.xlsx (preliminary bands)

Next steps / timeline:
- Ben (cc’d) will follow up with the technical note by EOD Tue 11/17.
- Marissa (cc’d) will put a Dedicated vs Private commercial term sheet into DocuSign draft by Thu 11/19.
- You confirm PHI / compliance constraint by Wed 11/18.

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up technical Q&A with your infra team for Thursday.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@healthapt.com>

Cc: Connor Leigh <connor.leigh@healthapt.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HealthApt deployment: tenancy & SLO clarification and next steps

Evelyn —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- PHI: yes, our long-term plan includes PHI. For the initial pilot we can run de-identified data but legal will only sign off if we have a clear path to Private/VPC or on-prem for PHI workloads.
- Noisy neighbor risk: our concern is not just throughput stalls — we need assurance that p99 latency spikes from unrelated tenants won't cause cascading timeouts in our downstream services. Can you quantify typical p99 increases on shared hosted under noisy conditions?
- Isolation boundary: we need a concise statement on what isolation guarantees exist for Dedicated vs Hosted. For Dedicated: are GPUs exclusively reserved to our workloads (i.e., single-tenant nodes) or pooled with soft isolation? For Private VPC: we need network-level data egress constraints and confirmation on key management integration (customer-managed KMS).

Also, can you provide the SOC2 or compliance artifacts we can share with Legal? Procurement will want an initial topline cost for Dedicated (monthly commit) vs Private (annual license + infra).

Thanks — if possible please get the technical note and SOC2 stub quickly; we'll prioritize a Thu tech call if Ben can do the deep dive.

Best,
Maria
Senior Engineering Manager, HealthApt

I’ll coordinate the Thu tech call for 11/19 09:00 PT if that works for their infra team.

Thanks — Evelyn

Maria — thanks for the clear list. Quick status and attachments to unblock Legal/Procurement: 

What I'm sending now (attached):
- SOC2-Type2-2026-stub.pdf (high-level SOC2 summary; legal requested the full audit — we’ll coordinate NDA/secure share for the full report).
- redwood_sla_and_tenancy_brief.pdf (short explainer comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private with SLO expectations).
- pricing-worksheet-healthapt.xlsx (topline bands for Dedicated vs Private).

Technical answers (summary):
- Hosted (shared): multi-tenant scheduler with continuous batching and soft intra-host isolation. GPUs are time-shared across tenants; in practice p99 can see variability under extreme load from other tenants. Typical observed p99 uplift in synthetic stress tests: 10–30% depending on model size and sequence lengths; we’ll include concrete plots in Ben’s note.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools by customer; nodes are logically dedicated to your workloads which eliminates noisy neighbor cross-talk at the host level. There remains shared control-plane components (routing, autoscaling) but data path and executor resources are tenant-reserved — Ben will provide exact wording for contract language.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, customer-managed KMS supported, and data egress controls. On-prem option removes our control-plane-dependent fallbacks and requires a slightly longer onboarding window (4–8 weeks typical).

Next steps / timeline recap:
- Ben: technical note + p50/p95/p99 plots by EOD Tue 11/17 (attached to the thread).
- Marissa: refined pricing and a short term sheet by Thu 11/19; will prepare a DocuSign.
- HealthApt: confirm PHI requirement and availability for Thu 11/19 09:00 PT tech call.

If you prefer, I can redact or mark sensitive pieces of the SOC2 stub before sending to Procurement.

Thanks — we’ll be ready to dig in on Thursday.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
